join_order.notes: 8 keyword ids; CSR fetches matching mk rows directly, yields (k_id, t_id) pairs

join_order.probe: cast_info via cast_info__movie_id offsets per surviving t_id
join_order.notes: Very selective LIKE; tiny set probed inside ci range per t_id
Direct bin lookup at t_id-1; ~5% pass year filter

data_structures.keyword_filter: flat_hash_set<int32_t> target_k_ids (cap 8) + vector<string> k_keyword_by_id keyed by k_id for MIN tracking
data_structures.t_id_dedupe: flat_hash_map<int32_t, int32_t> t_id -> best_k_id (smallest matching keyword string), pre-reserved ~200000
data_structures.min_tracking: three string buffers (movie_keyword, actor_name, hero_movie) updated lexicographically

parallelism.notes: Parallelize the 4.16M name LIKE scan across 12 threads with per-thread local sets merged at end. Keyword scan (134k) is serial. CSR expansion + ci probing is serial; total CSR/ci work is small after keyword filter.

notes: Track per-keyword string when building target_k_ids so MIN(k.keyword) reflects the actual matched k_id that produced an output row.
Dedupe t_id during CSR expansion: keep mapping t_id -> lexicographically smallest matching k.keyword string seen, to avoid re-probing cast_info for the same movie.

For each surviving (t_id, k_keyword_str): check production_year[t_id-1] > 2014 && != INT32_MIN; then iterate ci_off[t_id]..ci_off[t_id+1]; if any ci_person ∈ downey_robert_ids, update three MINs (resolve t.title from offsets, n.name from offsets, use stored k_keyword_str).

MIN(n.name) only needs to update with min over downey_robert_ids that actually appeared in a surviving match; track via per-match n.id, but since LIKE set is tiny, can precompute min name string offline and gate by membership in winning set; simplest: update MIN(n.name) on each accepted ci row.

Estimated final work: ~8 keyword ids -> a few thousand mk rows -> few thousand unique t_ids -> ~5% pass year -> short ci ranges with semi-join against ~50-element hash set. Total runtime dominated by parallel name LIKE scan.
